_comment: Cross-page consistency (ADR-1213). Every other lint in this lane reads ONE page's rendered
bytes, and three independent reader panels put a cross-page contradiction in their top four
findings -- so the worst defects the pages had were in the one place nothing could look.
A claim is a commitment stated on more than one page. The rule is not that the pages use the
same words; it is that wherever a page makes the claim AT ALL, it states the same NUMBER,
taken from the same facts field. The real defect was subtler than a mismatch: the pricing
page stated the price-rise commitment with no number at all -- 'we tell you before your next
payment' -- while the terms page said 'at least 30 days before your next renewal'. Nothing
disagreed numerically because one side had no number to disagree with, and the vaguer page
was the one a buyer reads before paying.
So the check is: on every page listed, the rendered value of `fact` must appear. A page that
makes the commitment vaguely fails, which is the point.

claims.what: how many days before a price rise takes effect you are told
how many days before an automatic charge you are told the amount and date
the length of the change-of-mind refund window
how long access continues after a payment fails or an invoice goes unpaid
how long live data takes to delete
